title: Air-Fryer Sausages
subtitle: Perfectly cooked pork sausages from the air fryer
excerpt: Pork sausages cooked in the air fryer until evenly browned all over with no splitting or burnt ends. The easiest way to cook sausages without any turning or watching.

recipe.sourceNotes: The air fryer is arguably the best way to cook sausages at home. The circulating hot air browns the sausages evenly on all sides without the need to turn them, and the fat renders into the drip tray rather than pooling in a pan and causing flare-ups. There is no risk of burnt ends and pale middles. The skins stay intact if the temperature is kept below 200 C.

content.text: There is no need to prick the sausages. The skins are better left intact: the fat stays inside and keeps the sausages moist. Do not exceed 190 C or the skins may split before the inside is cooked. Turn the sausages once halfway through cooking. They are ready when dark golden all over and the juices run clear.
Preheat the air fryer to 190 C for 2 minutes. Place the sausages in the basket in a single layer, spaced slightly apart.
Cook at 190 C for 7 minutes. Turn the sausages over. Cook for a further 7 to 8 minutes until deep golden all over.
Check the juices run clear before serving. Larger sausages may need an extra 2 to 3 minutes.
